title: About Me
text:
As an urban designer, I’m passionate about exploring the potential of public space and analyzing how it intersects with climate resilience, social equity, and user needs. My journey began with a desire to solve real-world problems with a design mindset, leading me to work in diverse locations such as China, Brazil, and various parts of the United States. I believe in working closely with communities to understand their concerns and implement locally-based solutions that truly make a difference.
When I create a design, it’s crucial to make it unique yet replicable. This requires a deep analysis of the special conditions of each site, while always keeping in mind the general ideas of balancing social, economic, and environmental needs. My goal is to craft designs that are both innovative and sustainable, contributing positively to the well-being of communities and the planet.

Welcome to my portfolio for MUSA 5080: Public Policy Analytics at the University of Pennsylvania.
This site documents my work in the Master of Urban Spatial Analytics program — weekly notes, course assignments, and a final project applying data analysis to urban policy questions.



I’m a student in the MCP program at Penn. My background is in urban planning and data science, and I’m interested in urban design, climate change adaptation, and making maps that inform decisions.
